title: The Chess Player Appears
next_chapter_hook: In the depths of that gaze that transcended time and space, a silhouette both achingly familiar and utterly alien flickered into view—it was Mo Xiansheng's form, yet not entirely. His voice was like destiny itself whispering: 'Chen Ji, you've finally arrived at this step.'

text.content:
The light at the end of the passage was not the blazing brilliance he had anticipated, but rather an eerie coldness that made his soul tremble. This illumination originated not from any visible source, but seeped through from some deeper, more ancient dimension—observing the abyss through a thin veil.

Chen Ji's feet stopped abruptly.

Because he saw it—the so-called 'Eye of Heavenly Dao,' now suspended in the void, entwined with countless threads of causality. These threads were not of its own weaving, but descended from a higher dimension, like the strings of a puppeteer controlling its every movement.

'This is impossible...' Beside Chen Ji, Chen Jie's voice trembled for the first time. 'The Eye of Heavenly Dao, the incarnation of Heavenly Dao's will in the mortal realm—how could it be a puppet?'

Chen Ji did not respond. In his pupils, the fragments of the Tianji Record flickered madly, yet could only capture a chaotic, blurred image—not because his connection with Chen Nian was disturbed, but because that 'higher existence' controlling the puppet simply did not exist within the river of fate that the Tianji Record could peer into.

dialogue.content:
'You have arrived.'

The Eye of Heavenly Dao's voice rang out, no longer the cold arrogance from before. Its tone now carried something eerily... compliant? No, not compliant—it was more like a pre-set program executing its final instructions.

'Ten thousand years,' it continued. 'Finally, someone can reach this place.'

Chen Ji narrowed his eyes. He noticed that as the Eye of Heavenly Dao spoke, those countless threads of causality all trembled slightly, as if someone in a higher dimension was manipulating its vocal cords.

'Finally?' he said slowly, his voice terrifyingly calm. 'I think you've been waiting more anxiously than us.'

The Eye of Heavenly Dao—or rather, the existence controlling it—fell silent for a moment. Then it spoke words that sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine:

'You're right. Compared to you, I do hope this moment arrives sooner. After all...' its voice suddenly became hollow and mechanical, 'I am merely a chess piece as well.'

text.content:
Chess—piece—

These two words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. He stared intently at the Eye of Heavenly Dao's massive pupil, seeing no longer the lofty judge, but a prisoner trapped upon a divine throne.

The source of those threads of causality finally became faintly visible through the fragments of Chen Ji's Tianji Record. It was not any existence he had encountered before—not Ling Yuan, not the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, not even any ancient great power he had long suspected.

It was something more fundamental.

'Fate,' Chen Ji heard his own voice, low and hoarse. 'Or rather—the very act of fate writing itself.'

Chen Jie whirled to look at him, eyes full of disbelief. 'What do you mean?'

Chen Ji did not answer. His fingers trembled slightly in his sleeves, not from fear, but from a deeper shock surging within him. The Tianji Record—he had always believed this was his sole reliance for peering into heavenly secrets. But now he understood.

The Tianji Record itself was merely one of the chess pieces of that higher existence.

dialogue.content:
'Let me guess.'

Chen Ji stepped forward, his voice conversely recovering that familiar languidness and calm. The corner of his mouth even curved into a smile—that smile none had ever seen when he orchestrated someone's death—cold, impossibly cold.

'Ten thousand years ago, there was a list.' he articulated each word distinctly. 'Everyone on that list was a chess piece chosen to execute some plan. And the Eye of Heavenly Dao was... another chess piece, responsible for overseeing the chessboard.'

He raised his head, gazing directly into the Eye of Heavenly Dao's massive pupil: 'Am I correct? Hea—ven—ly—Dao—Eye?'

The Eye of Heavenly Dao fell silent.

The silence stretched on for so long that Chen Jie couldn't help but want to urge him to speak. Then, the Eye of Heavenly Dao laughed.

That laughter emerged from the depths of its pupil, carrying an emotion that transcended anger and fear: 'Chen Ji. You truly have not disappointed me.'

'But you are wrong.' its voice suddenly turned sharp, 'I am not the chess piece overseeing the chessboard—I am the chessboard itself. And you have always been placing your pieces upon me.'

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

The chessboard itself?

If the Eye of Heavenly Dao was the chessboard, then the one playing the game...

Just then, he felt it.

It was an indescribable sensation—as if a gaze was watching him from somewhere beyond time and space. That gaze carried no malice, even bearing a kind of... appreciation?

'Chen Ji.'

A voice suddenly rang out in his mind. The voice was so familiar his heart clenched tightly—it was Mo Xiansheng's voice, yet somehow different. Older, more profound, as if having traversed endless rivers of time.

'See it now?' the voice asked. 'This is the truth you've always sought to find. The list from ten thousand years ago, the existence that laid out everything—'

'Who are you?' Chen Ji roared in his heart.

The voice fell silent for a moment, then let out a sigh: 'I am Mo Xiansheng. But I am also... part of fate itself. Chen Ji, do you wish to know the truth? Or are you afraid to know the truth?'

text.content:
"Speak." Chen Ji uttered a single word in his heart, his voice cold as if emerging from the Nine Abyssal Depths. "I, Chen Ji, have been scheming across the world for so many years. If I lack the courage to know the truth, then I am merely a joke."

The voice returned, carrying a hint of approval: "Good. This is why I chose you."

Then Chen Ji saw it—in that dimension beyond time and space, an image slowly emerged. The roster from ten thousand years ago was no ordinary roster. It was a "Genealogy of Fate"—recording all the chess pieces selected by Heavenly Will, as well as... the name of the chess player.

And that name, Chen Ji had seen before. On the night he obtained the Tianji Record Fragment, that name had flickered through his mind—the character "Mo." "Mo." "Mo..."

dialogue.content:
"Yes." Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his mind. "I am Mo. But I am also one of the architects of that catastrophe ten thousand years ago. The Tianji Record was the first work I refined—an original weapon meant to oppose a certain existence. But later..."

He fell silent for a moment, and for the first time, a hint of exhaustion entered his voice: "Later, I discovered that I too had become a chess piece. The fate written by fate—even the writers themselves cannot escape."

Chen Ji felt a wave of dizziness. It wasn't physical vertigo, but rather his entire framework of understanding collapsing and reorganizing. Mo Xiansheng—that existence he had believed to be an ally, that remnant soul who had always appeared as a guardian—had actually been one of the architects of the endgame ten thousand years ago?

"You knew about me from the very beginning." Chen Ji's voice trembled, but not from fear—it was from rage. "You knew I would obtain the Tianji Record, you knew I would come here, you even knew I would discover the truth—none of this was arranged by you?"

Mo Xiansheng did not deny it. "Yes. But Chen Ji, you must understand something—" his voice suddenly became incomparably gentle, "I arranged you, yet I have been waiting for a person capable of breaking this arrangement. And that person... is only you."

text.content:
"Break your arrangement?" Chen Ji coldly laughed. "What kind of joke are you making—"

Before he could finish, he suddenly stopped.

Because he realized something.

If Mo Xiansheng truly could arrange everything, then he should have been controlled so tightly that he wouldn't have any room for resistance. But in reality, he was standing here right now, able to question Mo Xiansheng, able to contemplate "breaking the arrangement" itself.

What did this indicate?

"You gave me the ability to think beyond your settings." Chen Ji said quietly. "So you're not controlling me—you are... guiding me?"

A hint of a smile entered Mo Xiansheng's voice: "You finally understand. I am not your enemy, Chen Ji. I am another person who wishes to break this chess game. And you—I am the only piece I have found that might succeed—or rather, a chess player."

"Chess player."

This word stirred a tempest in Chen Ji's heart.

He had always believed he was the chess player, believed the Tianji Record was his reliance to turn the tide in chaotic times. But now he understood—the true game was far grander than he had imagined, and the so-called "chess players" were merely chess pieces on another board.

But this did not mean despair.

On the contrary, when Chen Ji saw through all of this, an unprecedented calm rose in his heart. It was the calm of one who had stepped outside the board to view the game, the composure that only comes from seeing the entire picture.

"So," he slowly spoke, his voice carrying a determination that surprised even himself, "what do you want me to do?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then said: "I want you... to become a true chess player. Not a piece of Heavenly Dao, not a piece of fate—but an existence that transcends all of this."

"How to transcend?"

"Destroy the chessboard." Mo Xiansheng's voice turned ice-cold and resolute. "Destroy the existing Heavenly Dao order, rewrite fate. And the incomplete Tianji Record in your hands—is the only key that can accomplish this."

"Destroy the Heavenly Dao order."

These six characters were enough to drive any normal person insane. Chen Ji was no exception. But he quickly suppressed the shock in his heart and began to analyze all of this with a strategist's instinct.

"Is this the reason you chose me?" he asked. "Because I have the Tianji Record?"

"Not only that." Mo Xiansheng said. "The Tianji Record is merely a tool. What truly made me choose you was your disposition—that kind of determination to scheme even when in a desperate situation, that kind of madness to overturn the board even as a chess piece."

He paused, and a complex emotion entered his voice: "And also your obsession with Chen Nian. That kind of obsession—it is a truth that no calculation can simulate. And truth—is the only force capable of opposing fate."

Chen Ji fell silent.

He thought of Chen Nian, thought of his sister who had been missing for years but remained his greatest weakness. If destroying the Heavenly Dao order could find her—if this was what Mo Xiansheng had long anticipated—

"You are exploiting my feelings for Chen Nian." he said quietly.

"Yes." Mo Xiansheng frankly admitted. "But without these feelings, you would not have come this far. Our cooperation is a mutual exchange of needs."

"Each takes what they need."

Chen Ji chewed on these four words, then suddenly laughed.

That smile even surprised himself—not his usual mockery, not the timidity he feigned when pretending to be atrash, but a kind of近乎crazed的、狂妄的笑。

"Good." he said, "Each takes what they need. Since you're being so frank, then I won't hold back either."

He took a step forward,直视那天道之眼背后的虚空: "You said to make me a true执棋者—then let me ask you one question."

"Ask."

"If I destroy the天道秩序 and rewrite fate—" His voice turned cold, "What would happen to you?"

Silence.

Endless silence.

Then Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again,带着某种relieved的意味: "I would disappear. As part of the old order, I would cease to exist."

"What's in it for you?"

"Freedom." For the first time, genuine emotion crept into Mo Xiansheng's voice, "Ten thousand years, Chen Ji. I've been trapped in this残魂 for too long. If a new order can be born, then at least... I can rest in peace."

Rest in peace.

The word, from a being who had been plotting for ten thousand years, felt 重得格外heavy.

Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened them again, something unprecedented burned in his gaze.

"Deal." he said.

"Deal." Mo Xiansheng responded.

In that moment, an无形契约 was forged beyond time and space. Chen Ji felt his Heavenly Fate Value drain by a full thirty points—Tianji Record had主动响应了这份契约.

But at the same time, he felt an unprecedented power awakening within him. This was a side of Tianji Record never before revealed—not peeking into fate, but writing it.

"Go now, Chen Ji." Mo Xiansheng's voice began to fade, "You still have much to do. Tianqing Sect's Ling Yuan is merely the first obstacle, Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie merely the second. The true chess game has only just begun—"

"Wait." Chen Ji suddenly spoke, "Before I destroy the天道秩序, I have one more question."

"Ask."

"Chen Nian—where is she?"

Mo Xiansheng's voice fell silent for a moment, then gave an answer that made Chen Ji's heart stop:

"She is right by your side. From the very beginning, she has been by your side. You simply haven't found the method to awaken her yet."

The voice faded, leaving only these words echoing in Chen Ji's mind.

Chen Nian—right by his side?

He turned sharply, looking at Chen Jie—那个被他从幻境中救出、与他同名的mysterious存在 standing silently beside him.

"You—"

At that moment, Chen Jie raised her head and met his gaze. For the first time, something familiar flickered in those eyes—something that made Chen Ji's heart squeeze tight.

"Brother."

That single call, light as if穿越万年前, yet heavy enough to cause Chen Ji's entire world to collapse and rebuild.

text.content:
"Enough."

Chen Ji coldly spoke in his heart, cutting off Mo Xiansheng's words. His voice carried no emotion, yet radiated an suffocating pressure: "You've said so much, yet始终没有回答我最想问的问题."

"What question?"

"Who exactly are you?" Chen Ji's voice变得危险, "A残魂 guarding the Tianji Record Fragment, how could it possibly possess power beyond the Heavenly Eye? You say you're not an enemy—but would an enemy's face read 'I am the enemy' in four big characters?"

Silence.

In that超越时空的注视, something Chen Ji recognized appeared for the first time—surprise.

"You truly are different from others." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a complex tone, "No, you're smarter than everyone. Chen Ji, you're right. My identity is indeed more than just a残魂守护者."

"Then clarify." Chen Ji pressed relentlessly, "The list from ten thousand years ago, your布局 within the Tianji Record, the real reason you chose me—tell me everything. Otherwise—"

His lips curved into a cold smile: "Otherwise I'll turn around and leave right now. I've already learned about the Heavenly Eye's puppet nature. I'll investigate the remaining truth myself. Your help, I don't need."

Mo Xiansheng fell into a long silence.

That silence almost made Chen Ji think the other would give up. Then, that voice beyond time and space rang out again, this time carrying aheavy、不得不说的意味.

"Fine. Since you want to know, I'll tell you."

"The great catastrophe ten thousand years ago was not a natural disaster, but a struggle." Mo Xiansheng's voice deepened, "The object of contention was control over the天道. At that time, three forces participated in this struggle—the order faction represented by the Heavenly Eye, the chaos faction represented by the魔道 Holy Sect, and..."

He paused, voice turning bitter: "And the third force I belonged to—we wanted to completely destroy the old天道 and establish a brand new order."

"You lost." Chen Ji断言.

"Yes." Mo Xiansheng didn't deny, "We lost badly. The order faction won, establishing the current天道体系. Those of us who failed were either erased or sealed—I am the latter."

"But you survived." Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, "As a残魂, parasitic within the Tianji Record, waiting for the next opportunity."

"To be precise, waiting for someone capable of breaking the old order." A glimmer of hope entered Mo Xiansheng's voice, "And you are that person."

Chen Ji did not respond immediately.

He was calculating rapidly. Mo Xiansheng's words sounded very reasonable—the defeated's revenge, the shattered Tianji Record, the waiting remnant soul—but it was all too reasonable. Reasonable to the point of sounding like a prepared script.

"You say you want to break the old order," he said slowly. "Then let me ask you—what comes after breaking it? What kind of new order do you want to establish?"

"That depends on your choice," Mo Xiansheng replied.

"My choice?"

"Yes." Mo Xiansheng's voice became solemn. "One of the reasons we failed ten thousand years ago was that our internal ideological divisions were too severe. Some wanted to establish absolute order, others wanted absolute freedom, and in the end, we shattered into pieces. And this time—"

He paused: "I will not make the same mistake. The form of the new order will be determined by you. I am only responsible for providing strength and knowledge—everything else will be left to you."

Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "That sounds beautiful. But why should I trust you?"

"Because you have no other choice." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a hint of resignation. "I know you don't trust me. But Chen Ji, you are already in this chess game. The only question is—do you want to be a chess piece, or do you want to be the chess player?"

This sentence made Chen Ji fall into silence.

Yes, whether he trusted Mo Xiansheng or not, he was already in this chess game. The existence of the Tianji Record, the puppet nature of the Heavenly Eye, Chen Nian's disappearance, Ling Yuan's ambitions—everything pointed to the same truth: this chess game was far larger than he had imagined, and he was already a player within it.

The question was, did he want to continue being a passive chess piece, or did he want to take the initiative and become the chess player?

"I need time to consider," he finally said.

"Of course." Mo Xiansheng did not seem surprised. "But time is running out. The Heavenly Eye has already been exposed about its puppet nature, and the existence behind it will soon notice. Before that—"

"Before that what?"

"Before that, you need to make a choice." Mo Xiansheng's voice became meaningful. "Whether to continue being my collaborator, to become my enemy—or to simply become a third force yourself."

"Third force?"

"Yes. Stepping out from behind both my faction and your faction, becoming your own chess player." A note of approval appeared in Mo Xiansheng's voice. "To be honest, I have been waiting for you to say this."

A thought stirred in Chen Ji's heart.

The third force—this was precisely what he wanted most. Not a chess piece to be used, not a passive allied collaborator, but an existence independent of all factions.

"What can you give me?" he asked directly.

"The complete transmission of the Tianji Record." Mo Xiansheng answered without hesitation. "I can only give you a portion now, but if you are willing, I can gradually unseal more knowledge—including the complete truth of the catastrophe ten thousand years ago, and the true operating mechanism of the Heavenly Order."

"What is the price?"

"Each time you unseal it, your Heavenly Fate value will be consumed more." Mo Xiansheng said candidly. "But in exchange, you need to help me accomplish one thing."

"What thing?"

"Find Chen Nian."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply: "You know where Chen Nian is?"

"I know." Mo Xiansheng's voice softened. "It is true that she was taken by the Holy Sect, but her current state... she is not a prisoner, but rather... a sacrifice."

Sacrifice?

This word made Chen Ji's blood almost freeze.

"What kind of sacrifice?" His voice became dangerous. "A sacrifice to whom?"

"To the existence behind the Heavenly Eye." Mo Xiansheng said. "That existence requires a large amount of Heavenly Fate power to sustain its existence, and Chen Nian—she is the Heavenly Fate Key, the most perfect Heavenly Fate vessel. If she is sacrificed..."

He did not finish, but Chen Ji already understood.

If Chen Nian was sacrificed, she would vanish completely. Not death, but something more terrifying than death—being integrated into the Heavenly Order, becoming part of the machinery that maintains the old order's operation, forever unable to be retrieved.

"Tell me." Chen Ji's voice became ice-cold and calm, a coldness never seen before even by those who had witnessed his lethal schemes. "Where is the Holy Sect? Where is Chen Nian?"

"The Holy Sect is in the extreme cold lands of the northern region." Mo Xiansheng said. "But I must warn you—with your current strength, rushing directly into the Holy Sect is only a dead end. You need more power."

"What kind of power?"

"The complete transmission of the Tianji Record." Mo Xiansheng repeated. "Only when you have completely mastered the power of the Tianji Record will you have the qualification to challenge the Holy Sect and rescue Chen Nian."

Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then raised his head. The light in his eyes made even the Heavenly Eye tremble involuntarily.

"Good." he said. "I accept your conditions. But there is one prerequisite—"

"Speak."

"From now on, I am no longer your chess piece." Chen Ji said word by word. "We are in a cooperative relationship, but I am not under your command. You provide knowledge and strength, I decide how to use them—this is my bottom line."

After a moment of silence, Mo Xiansheng laughed.

That laughter carried a sense of relief, even a trace of gratification: "Good. This is the person I chose."

The contract was forged.

Chen Ji felt the Tianji Record within him tremble slightly, as the connection between him and Mo Xiansheng became deeper. At the same time, an unprecedented power was surging from the depths of the Tianji Record—the complete transmission was slowly unsealing.

"Now," Mo Xiansheng's voice began to become distant, "you have one final thing to do."

"What?"

"Face the puppet master behind the Heavenly Eye." Mo Xiansheng's voice became serious. "It has already sensed the anomaly. Before it makes a move, you need to strike first—let the puppet know that even its master is merely a chess piece."

Chen Ji raised his head and looked toward the void behind the Heavenly Eye. He knew that within that void, a higher-dimensional existence was watching all of this.

And he was about to declare war on that existence, in the identity of a chess player.

"Interesting." he murmured, a dangerous smile curving at the corner of his mouth. "After laying out this game for so many years, it's time to let those lurking in the shadows taste the滋味 of being outmaneuvered."

"If you were the kind of existence that surrendered easily, I would be disappointed." The voice said, "What I await is not a compliant vessel, but an existence capable of truly challenging the Heavenly Dao. Only such an existence is qualified to become my... successor."

Successor?

Chen Ji narrowed his eyes: "You want me to devour you?"

"Not devouring, but fusion." The voice corrected, "I will impart all my knowledge and power to you, and you will inherit my will—to break the old Heavenly Dao and establish a new order."

"That sounds wonderful." Chen Ji said coldly, "But what is the price?"

"The price is—you will no longer be 'Chen Ji.'" The voice said calmly, "Your consciousness will be overwritten. You will become a new 'me.' Your memories, your obsessions, your Chen Nian—all will cease to exist."

The air seemed to freeze.

Chen Ji's fists slowly clenched within his sleeves. This choice was too cruel—saving Chen Nian's price was losing himself?

"Is there another choice?" he asked.

"There is." The voice said, "You can refuse. But the price of refusal is—you will fall here today, and Chen Nian will become someone else's sacrifice."

It paused, and temptation crept into its voice: "There is a third choice—before I truly descend, destroy this puppet and cause my plan to fail. But that also means you will forever lose the chance to obtain the complete Tianji Record, and never save Chen Nian."

Three choices, each an impasse.

Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened them again, something unprecedented burned in those eyes—it was the light of madness, and also the light of reason.

"I choose the fourth." he said.

"What?" For the first time, confusion entered the voice.

"You said you waited three thousand years for an answer." Chen Ji slowly spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm, "Then I will give you an answer—"

He abruptly raised his head, confronting that Void beyond time and space: "I will break your chess game without becoming your successor. I will obtain the complete Tianji Record without having my will overwritten. I will save Chen Nian without sacrificing myself."

"That's impossible—"

"Whether it's possible or not," Chen Ji interrupted, "is not for you to decide."

His voice turned ice-cold and resolute: "You've miscalculated one thing—I, Chen Ji, have been scheming across the world for so many years, and I never believe in any 'no choice' ending. Every seemingly hopeless situation hides a third path."

"Where does your confidence come from?" the voice asked with a hint of amusement.

Chen Ji smiled faintly and took something from his sleeve.

It was—the final fragmentary page of the Tianji Record.

"This is my confidence." he said, "You think you've been waiting for me—but in truth, I have also been waiting for you."

The voice fell silent.

A true, complete silence.

Chen Ji felt his heart racing, but he forced himself to remain calm. He knew he was gambling a grand gamble—that the fragmentary page could become his trump card for a reversal.

"Where did you obtain it?" The voice finally spoke, no longer the lofty examination from before, but carrying genuine surprise.

"Guess." Chen Ji said.

Silence.

Then, the voice let out a low laugh: "Mo Xiansheng... so that's how it is. He has been betraying me all along."

Chen Ji said nothing. Yes, this was all Mo Xiansheng's layout—表面上 he appeared to be the chess piece of that terrifying existence, but secretly he had been helping Chen Ji obtain that crucial fragmentary page.

"What is that fragmentary page?" the voice asked, "I actually cannot see through it."

Chen Ji smiled faintly: "This is my trump card. You want to devour me? Then try catching me before I use this fragmentary page."

Before the words finished, he abruptly activated that fragmentary page.

In an instant, a brilliant light erupted from his palm—that light was not an attack, but something deeper, more essential. It pierced through time, through space, through causality, directly acting upon fate itself.

"This is—" For the first time, terror entered the voice, "Foresight technique?! No, this is even more terrifying—this is—"

"This is rewriting." Chen Ji's voice echoed within the light, "The true power of the Tianji Record—not to peer into fate, but to rewrite fate."

The light enveloped the entire space.

Chen Ji felt his Heavenly Fate Value draining madly—50 points, 80 points, 100 points—but he gritted his teeth and persevered, because he knew this was his only chance.

Rewrite fate.

What he wanted to rewrite was nothing else—but his own identity.

That terrifying existence called him "the most perfect chess piece," "the most perfect vessel"—so he would break this definition. He would make himself no longer a chess piece, no longer a vessel, but the true—Chess Player.

The light gradually faded.

Chen Ji knelt on the ground, drenched in sweat. His Heavenly Fate Value had dropped to a dangerous edge, but an unprecedented light burned in his eyes.

Because he had succeeded.

In that instant, he had rewritten his fate—he was no longer the chess piece of that terrifying existence, no longer a slave to the Tianji Record, no longer a character in anyone else's scheme.

He was Chen Ji.

The one and only, irreplaceable existence that transcended all calculations.

"You—" The voice sounded, no longer from the Void, but right beside his ear, "What exactly are you?"

Chen Ji slowly stood up, raised his head, and confronted that gaze beyond time and space. A faint smile curved his lips—that smile held no mockery, no coldness, only a pure, transcendent sense of—

"I am Chen Ji." he said, "And you, starting today, are no longer the Chess Player—but the next opponent I will defeat."

result_nodes.description: Regardless of who you are, regardless of how long you've waited—I, Chen Ji, despise being used as a chess piece more than anything in this life. Since you want to play, let's play a big game. Tear everything apart directly and see who emerges as the final victor.

text.content:
"Three thousand years of waiting?"

Chen Ji's voice suddenly rang out, interrupting the terrifying existence's monologue. A cold smile curled at the corner of his mouth, carrying a dangerous edge: "Touching story. But have you ever considered—"

He abruptly raised his head, staring directly at the Void: "I've been waiting for this moment for just as long."

The voice clearly faltered: "You... what do you mean?"

"What I mean is," Chen Ji spoke word by word, "you thought you were setting a trap for me? Wrong. From the moment I obtained the Tianji Record, I've been laying a trap for you."

He slowly drew from his sleeve the fragment he'd kept hidden—the seventh page of the Tianji Record, its final incomplete page: "You thought the Tianji Record was a gift you bestowed upon me? Wrong. The Tianji Record was the bait I used to lure you out."

The atmosphere in the air shifted abruptly.

The terrifying existence's will condensed violently, taking on a dangerous aura: "You're bluffing?"

"Whether I'm bluffing or not—why not test it and find out?" Chen Ji's smile grew even deeper, "After manipulating the world for so many years, if I didn't know how to draw out the snake, I might as well go back to farming."

He paused, his voice turning cold and dangerous: "You want a 'perfect vessel,' don't you? Then come and take it—if you have the ability."

Silence stretched for a moment.

Then, the terrifying existence laughed.

That laughter carried a twisted sense of delight: "Good. Good one, Chen Ji."

Its voice turned dangerous and fanatical: "You think you've prepared some hidden trump card? The Tianji Record fragment? Or Mo Xiansheng's betrayal?"

Chen Ji offered no response, merely watching the Void quietly.

"I'll tell you," the voice said, "all your preparations are worthless before me. Because I am—"

"What are you?" Chen Ji suddenly interrupted, his tone carrying a hint of playfulness, "A fool who was betrayed by Mo Xiansheng, outmaneuvered by me, yet still preening with satisfaction?"

The air seemed to freeze.

The terrifying existence's will surged violently, bringing with it pressure enough to tear through space: "You—!"

"Me what?" Chen Ji showed not a trace of fear, instead laughing even more happily, "You waited three thousand years, only to end up a fool who didn't even notice Mo Xiansheng's betrayal. Tell me, weren't those three thousand years a complete waste?"

He deliberately sighed: "What a pity. I thought you might give me some challenge. I never expected—"

He shook his head, his tone brimming with disappointment: "Nothing special, after all."

This was naked humiliation.

Blatant humiliation of that terrifying existence that claimed to have waited three thousand years.

"Chen—Ji—!"

True fury entered that voice. No longer the lofty scrutiny, no longer the composure of one playing with chess pieces—true rage, thefurious of one who had been humiliated.

"I will make you pay the price!"

Before the words even finished, a world-destroying force descended from the Void, lunging directly toward Chen Ji.

But Chen Ji laughed.

More brilliantly than ever before.

"Finally angry." He murmured, "I've been waiting for you to lose your temper."

The moment that force was about to touch him, he abruptly activated the seventh page of the Tianji Record—the final trump card secretly left for him by Mo Xiansheng.

A brilliant light erupted, directly tearing apart that terrifying force.

"Impossible—!" The voice shrieked in disbelief.

"Nothing is impossible." Chen Ji's voice echoed within the light, "I told you—you forgot one thing."

"What?"

A bloodthirsty smile curled at Chen Ji's mouth: "After manipulating the world for so many years, I never play by the rules. You think you're on the fifth level, but I'm actually on the seventh."

The light faded.

Chen Ji still stood where he was, while the terrifying existence's will had been temporarily suppressed.

"This is only the beginning." Chen Ji murmured, "You waited three thousand years, didn't you? Then I'll make you wait three thousand years too—until you have another chance to deal with me."

He turned and looked at Chen Jie, who had been silently standing beside him: "Let's go."

"Wait—" Chen Jie started, his eyes carrying a complicated expression.

"There's nothing to wait for." Chen Ji cut him off, his voice brooking no argument, "Today's purpose has been achieved. We know who the enemy is, we know his weakness—the rest, we'll discuss after returning."

He cast one final glance at the Void, a meaningful smile playing at his lips: "The next time we meet, I'll show you what a true chess player looks like."

With that, he walked toward the passage exit without looking back.

Behind him, the terrifying existence's furious roar echoed throughout the space: "Chen Ji—! I will make you pay the price—!"

But Chen Ji simply waved his hand, as if shooing away a fly.

"Remember to bring some proper trump cards next time." His voice drifted back, "A three-thousand-year-old antique who can't even deal with a newcomer—truly bringing shame to the Heavens."

result_nodes.description: Not rushing to take a stance. This existence has said too much, the information overload—Chen Ji needs time to digest and analyze, to find the gaps and flaws in the other party's words. To plan and then act—that is his style.

text.content:
Chen Ji did not speak.

He merely stood there quietly, appearing to be listening on the surface, while his mind raced at lightning speed.

Three thousand years of waiting. The most perfect piece. The vessel. The inheritor.

These words tumbled repeatedly through his mind, piecing together an increasingly clear picture.

First, was what this existence said true? Not necessarily. After so many years of setting up schemes across the world, he knew too well that "information" itself was the most dangerous weapon. The other party claimed to be the creator of the Tianji Record—but who could say if that was true or false?

Second, even if it were true, so what? Even if he was the creator of the Tianji Record, it only proved he had been powerful once—it did not mean he remained powerful now. Three thousand years was enough time for any existence to change.

Third, and most critically—he called Mo Xiansheng a "traitor." What did that mean? It meant Mo Xiansheng did not stand completely on this existence's side. It meant he had a potential ally, someone secretly helping him without this existence's knowledge.

Fourth...

Chen Ji's eyes narrowed slightly.

Fourth, this existence said "vessel" not "tool." A vessel is used to hold things—so what exactly did he want to hold? His entire will? His soul? Or something else?

If it were the latter, it meant this existence was seeking a replacement. He did not want to use Chen Ji's power, but wanted to...possess Chen Ji's body?

This speculation sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine.

But at the same time, it also made his thoughts clearer.

"You claim to be the creator of the Tianji Record." Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice calm without any emotion. "Then you should know what the Tianji Record's greatest flaw is."

That voice seemed unprepared for this question, pausing briefly before answering: "Flaw? The Tianji Record is perfect—"

"No." Chen Ji interrupted. "The Tianji Record's greatest flaw is that it can only see fate, but cannot change fate."

He paused, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly: "You said I saw things I shouldn't have seen. But in truth, every vision I saw was already a projection of the 'past.' The essence of the Tianji Record is a mirror—it can only reflect already existing fate, but cannot create new fate."

"So what?" that voice asked, seemingly intrigued by his analysis.

"So," Chen Ji stared directly at that void, "you said you waited three thousand years for an 'answer'—but what answer can a mirror that can only see but not change give you?"

Silence.

Real, complete silence.

Then that terrifying existence's laughter rang out—but no longer in a condescending manner, instead carrying a strange appreciation.

"You are indeed different from others." it said. "When others heard what I said, their first reaction was fear, anger, or submission. But you—you analyzed me."

"What's so strange about that?" Chen Ji shrugged. "I'm a strategist. Analysis is my instinct."

"But you're more than a strategist." that voice grew serious. "You're the first existence I've encountered in three thousand years who can calmly analyze me. Others are pieces, but you—"

It paused, and a meaningful tone entered its voice: "You're a true chess player."

"So what?"

"So, I've changed my mind." that voice said. "I don't need a vessel. I need a—collaborator."

Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "Collaborate?"

"Yes." that voice became solemn. "I provide knowledge and power, you provide...a unique perspective. Together, we break the existing heavenly order and establish a new pattern."

"Sounds wonderful." Chen Ji said. "But what do I get out of it?"

"Anything you want." that voice said. "Power, strength, immortality—even your sister's life."

Chen Nian.

This name made Chen Ji's heart clench tightly. But he forced himself to maintain a calm expression: "You know where Chen Nian is?"

"Of course." that voice carried a certain confidence. "I am the creator of the Tianji Record. I know the location of every existence ever recorded in the Tianji Record—including your sister."

"How is she now?"

"Still alive." that voice said. "But not for long. The Holy Sect is preparing a grand sacrifice—and Chen Nian is the offering. If you don't rescue her within three months, she will vanish completely."

Three months.

Chen Ji's fists slowly tightened within his sleeves. But his voice remained calm: "You're telling me this to make me agree to your terms?"

"Not terms." that voice corrected. "Collaboration. We are equals—I regard you as a collaborator, not a piece."

Chen Ji fell silent.

This was an extremely tempting proposal. With this existence's help, he truly might be able to rescue Chen Nian—but at what cost? He never believed in free lunches in this world.

"I need time to consider." he finally said.

"Of course." that voice did not seem surprised. "But time is running out. The Eye of Heavenly Dao will soon detect everything you've discovered. Before then, you must make a choice—"

"Become your collaborator, or become your enemy?"

"Exactly." that voice carried a strange smile. "I await your answer, Chen Ji."

The voice gradually faded, and that terrifying existence's will began to retreat.

But just before completely disappearing, it left one final sentence: "By the way, Mo Xiansheng asked me to tell you—he said the 'seventh page' is on you. Don't let it fall into my hands."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly.

The seventh page? That was the final missing piece of the Tianji Record—Mo Xiansheng had actually given it to him long ago?

He unconsciously reached into his sleeve, touching that fragment he had always ignored.

So that's how it was.

Mo Xiansheng had been scheming from the very beginning—ostensibly on that terrifying existence's side, but secretly helping him.

Chen Ji took a deep breath and slowly exhaled.

The situation was more complex than he imagined. The enemy was stronger than he imagined. But at the same time, the allies were also more numerous than imagined.

"Three months." he murmured. "That's enough."

He turned, looking at Chen Jie who had been silently standing beside him: "Let's go. We still have things to do."

Chen Jie nodded and followed his steps.

And behind them, that gaze from the void continued watching all of this—carrying amusement, anticipation, and a kind of twisted patience.

The three-thousand-year chess game had finally reached its most brilliant moment.

And Chen Ji was about to write his own legend in this game of chess.

The light and shadow of the passage receded behind Chen Ji, but that gaze transcending time and space never faded.

Chen Jie followed behind him, wanting to speak but holding back. Finally, he couldn't help but ask: 'You... really plan to cooperate with that existence?'

Chen Ji didn't look back, merely saying calmly: 'What do you think?'

'I think—' Chen Jie paused, 'you won't.'

'Oh? Why so certain?'

'Because of something you just said.' Chen Jie's voice turned serious, 'You said 'every seemingly hopeless situation hides a third path'. This doesn't sound like a spur-of-the-moment remark—it feels more like a belief you've always held.'

Chen Ji stopped walking.

He turned around, looking at Chen Jie—that mysterious existence with the same name as him. This person's observation skills were sharper than he'd imagined.

'You're right.' He spoke, his voice carrying a surprising frankness even to himself, 'I won't cooperate with that thing. At least—not according to the rules it has set.'

'Then what will you do?'

Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then took out from his sleeve that always-neglected fragment—the seventh page of the Tianji Record.

'Mo Xiansheng said something.' He murmured, 'He said 'every fragment of the Tianji Record is a door'. At the time I thought he was talking nonsense—but now I understand.'

He raised his head, his eyes gleaming with a dangerous light: 'This seventh page isn't for peeking at fate or rewriting it. It's a door—leading to a higher dimension.'

'You're saying—'

'What I'm saying,' Chen Ji interrupted, his voice turning cold and resolute, 'is that thing claims to be the creator of the Tianji Record, claims it waited three thousand years for a vessel—but it forgot one thing.'

'What thing?'

Chen Ji tucked the fragment back into his sleeve, a cold smile curling at his lips: 'It said the Tianji Record can only be observed, not changed. But it forgot—creator doesn't equal controller. I don't need to become its vessel or collaborator.'

He turned and strode forward: 'I only need to do one thing—seize ownership. Turn the Tianji Record from its creation into my possession.'

'Is that possible?' Chen Jie followed his steps, 'It's the creator of the Tianji Record—'

'Creators can also be devoured by their own creations.' Chen Ji's voice echoed through the passage, 'Do you think why Mo Xiansheng betrayed it? Why the fragments of the Tianji Record choose their own masters?'

He paused, his voice tinged with sarcasm: 'It's too confident. Confident enough to think it's the rule-maker—yet forgetting that rules are always meant to be broken.'

The footsteps gradually faded away.

From somewhere at the end of the passage, Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted faintly: 'You finally understand. But it's not enough—Chen Ji, the real trial has just begun.'

Chen Ji didn't respond.

He simply continued walking forward, his stride firm and resolute.

Because he knew from this moment, everything was different.

The Heavenly Eye's true nature as a puppet had been exposed.
The real幕后 chess master had stepped into the light.
And he, Chen Ji—no longer a piece, but about to become the chess player.

The three-month deadline had begun its countdown.
Chen Nian's crisis remained unresolved.
Ling Yuan's schemes still spread in the shadows.

But he was no longer afraid.

Because he finally understood one thing—

What they call fate is merely a bigger chess game.
And he—will become the one who overturns the board.

As Chen Ji's figure vanished at the end of the passage, something complex appeared in the enormous pupil of the Heavenly Eye for the first time.

Not anger.
Not fear.
But—admiration.

'Interesting.' A voice came from the void behind it, 'Truly very interesting.'

The Heavenly Eye slowly turned, as if conversing with some non-existent presence: 'Master, are you not worried?'

'Worried about what?' The voice carried a playful tone, 'Worried that he might find a way to break the chess game?'

'...Yes.'

A moment of silence.

Then the voice let out a low laugh—one carrying a twisted delight: 'No. I'm not worried. Quite the opposite—I am very much looking forward to it.'

'Looking forward to?'

'You wouldn't understand.' The voice grew low and fervent, 'Three thousand years of waiting, I've grown weary of pieces moving by the book. But this Chen Ji—he is a true variable. He gives me hope of breaking this boring cycle.'

'So you're going to go easy on him?'

'Not going easy.' The voice corrected, 'But giving him enough space to exert himself. If the pieces are too weak, the game becomes meaningless. But when the pieces are strong enough—'

Its voice carried a hint of anticipation: 'The game becomes magnificent.'

Behind the Heavenly Eye, that presence in the void seemed to smile: 'Go, have your puppet暂时 withdraw. Let Ling Yuan continue his schemes, let Han Lie continue his pursuit—I want to see how far this Chen Ji can go.'

'Understood.'

The light gradually faded, the Heavenly Eye restoring its high-and-mighty indifferent appearance—as if everything just now was merely an illusion.

And in a distant frozen palace in the northern realm's extreme cold lands, a figure bound by chains slowly opened her eyes.

They were eyes bearing some resemblance to Chen Ji's.

'Brother...' Her lips barely moved, her voice as light as a whisper, 'You've finally... begun to act...'

The chains clanked as she fell back into slumber.

But at the highest point of the ice palace, a pair of eyes watched her direction—those of Ye Qing, the Holy Sect's saintess of the Demonic Path.

'Chen Ji...' A complex smile curved her lips, 'You truly haven't disappointed me.'

The chessboard of fate has been set.
The chess players have taken their positions.
And the final victory or defeat—

Has just begun.

Tianqing Sect, Servants' Quarters.

Chen Ji sat in that dilapidated small room, before him on the table lay all the fragments of the Tianji Record. The candlelight flickered, casting his shadow on the wall, stretched long and long.

Chen Jie stood behind him, quietly gazing at those fragments.

"What are you going to do?" he asked.

Chen Ji did not answer immediately. His fingers gently brushed across those fragments, feeling the Heavenly Secrets Power flowing within them.

"Three months." He finally spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm. "That thing gave me three months. Not a gift, but a warning—it's telling me that if I can't make a choice within three months, it will choose for me."

"So you want to become stronger within three months?"

"No." Chen Ji shook his head. "Three months is too short. Hoping to clash head-on leads only to death. What I need to do is something else entirely."

He raised his head, his eyes flickering with a dangerous light: "I want to make it regret giving me three months."

"What do you mean?"

Chen Ji stood up, carefully collecting those fragments one by one: "That thing claimed to be the creator of the Tianji Record, said it waited three thousand years for a vessel—but it forgot one thing."

"What?"

Chen Ji turned around, a cold smirk curling at his lips: "It said the Tianji Record can only be observed, not altered. But it forgot—creator does not equal controller. I don't need to become its vessel or collaborator."

He paused, his voice turning ice-cold and resolute: "I only need to do one thing—"
